 J U D G M E N T
The Police Sub-Inspector, Bagalagunte PS submitted charge sheet against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 506, 307 of IPC.
2 . The brief story of the prosecution are as under:
The accused and complainant Lakshmamma's marriage performed on 26.06.1991.

After marriage, both have started to reside at No.2245, situated at 7 th cross, Ramesh Bagalgunte Ps vs Chowdappa on 29 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149266920/
1 road, T.Dasarahalli, Bengaluru.

The accused quarrelled with the complainant without any reasons and assaulting her and also made the cylinder to leak and abused her in filthy language and thereby committed criminal intimidation by subjecting her to physical and mental cruelty.
As such the complainant filed petition before the Family Court against the accused for divorce.

Due to which, the accused has enraged and on 13.04.2018 at 11.00 a.m when the complainant was on her way on public road situated beside Kaliyamma temple, T.Dasarahalli at that time, the accused with an intention to kill the complainant picked up quarrel by abusing in filthy language and tried to assault with machete (machu) on the left side of her neck, but the complainant escaped and brought her left hand and sustained injuries, if the complainant not brought her hand, then she would have succumbed to death and thereby committed the above said offences.

3. The concerned police have submitted charge sheet before the concerned Judicial Magistrate,
Bangalore.

The learned Magistrate, after taking cognizance of the offences against the accused,
committed the case to the Sessions Court by complying Section 207 of CrPC by furnishing copy of the charge sheet to the accused.

After committal, the said case was numbered as SC No. 431/2021.
4.

The charge was framed against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 506,
307 of IPC.
The accused has pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
5. The prosecution has examined eight witnesses as PWs.1 to 8 and got marked documents at EX.P1 to P10.
This court has issued summons, warrant and proclamation against CW.4 and C.W.5.

Inspite of that, the concerned police failed to execute and produce the said witnesses CW.4 and C.W.5 before the court, as such the prayer of the learned PP was rejected and C.W.4 and C.W.5 were dropped.
However liberty has been given to the prosecution for examination of the said witnesses, if the said witnesses brought before the court by the concerned police.

Moreover in the present case,
the prime witnesses of the prosecution were turned hostile.
6. After completion of prosecution side evidence, this court has recorded the statements of accused as provided under Section 313 of CrPC.
The accused has denied incriminating evidence present against him and not opted to lead defence evidence nor submitted anything to the court.
The accused has complied Section 437A of CrPC.

7. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials on record.
8.

The following points that arises for consideration of this court:
1. Whether the prosecution proves that on 26.06.1991 accused got married C.W.1,
later residing at No.2245, 7th cross, Ramesh road, T.Dasarahalli, Bengaluru and later quarrelling with the C.W.1 for silly reasons and assaulting her and made cylinder leak and subjected her to physical and mental cruelty and thereby accused has committed the offence punishable U/s.498A of Indian Penal Code, 1860?

sentences.text:
2. Whether the prosecution proves that the accused being the husband of CW.1 Lakshmamma, caused criminal intimidation to the deceased by threatening her &
thereby accused has committed an offence punishable under Section 506 of IPC?

3. Whether the prosecution proves that on 13.04.2018 at 11.00 a.m the accused with an intention and knowledge attempted to kill C.W.1, abused the C.W1 and thrown the iron machete on her left neck, immediately C.W.1 kept her left hand and escaped and thereby accused has committed an offence punishable U/s.307 of IPC?
4. What order?
9. This Court has answered the above above points are as under:
 Point No.1: In the Negative  Point No.2: In the Negative  Point No.3: In the Negative  Point No.4: As per final order  for the following:
 R E A S O N S 10.
Points No.1 to 3: All these points are taken up together for discussions as they are related with each other and to avoid repetition.
The prosecution has succeeded to examine 8 witnesses as PW.1 to P.W.8 and got marked documents Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10.
Among these 8 witnesses, the witnesses PW.1, P.W.3, P.W.4 and P.W.6 are the family members of the complainant.
The witness P.W.5 is the doctor, P.W.7 and P.W.8 are the police officers i.e. Investigation Officers.
To bring home the guilt against the accused, the prosecution examined the complainant Lakshmamma who is none other than the wife of the accused.
The evidence of said Lakshmamma discloses that there was oral exchange of words between her and accused due to the properties dispute and rent.
At that time, she was fell down and sustained injury to her left forehand and hand.
There was case pending before the family court, the said case was got compromised by the complainant and accused.
According to this witness, the complainant never gave any physical and mental harassment nor given threat to life nor assaulted with machete to the P.W.1- complainant.
However when she went to the police station, due to the oral exchange of words and differences between her and accused, at that time, the police have obtained her signatures on the documents.
As she fell down voluntarily, hence she went to Sanjeevini hospital for treatment.
So the evidence given by the star witness of the prosecution not in consonance with the recitals of the complaint and both Mahazar.
In fact the concerned police failed to obtain her signature on the Mahazar marked at Ex.P.3.
This also creates doubt about the conducting of the Mahazar by the concerned police at the place of incident and also at the residence of complainant.
It is very clear that the evidence of complainant present on record completely contrary to the documents marked at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.3.

3 11.

sentences.text:
In this case the prosecution has examined daughter, son and sister of the complainant as P.W.3,
P.W.6 and P.W.4 respectively.
The witness P.W.3 Chandini, P.W.4 Parvathamma and P.W.6 Shashikumar are being the daughter, sister and son of the complainant failed to depose about the incident as alleged against the accused.
According to these 3 witnesses, there was just oral exchange of words between accused and complainant with regard to rent.
Except that nothing has happened and the accused never subjected the complainant by any sort of physical and mental harassment nor assaulted her with machete.

The another prime witness of the prosecution by name Puttamma being the signatory to the Mahazar Ex.P.2 and witness to the incident also not support the prosecution story by deposing she was not the witness to the incident nor pacified the quarrel and rescued the complainant/injured.

It is no doubt the said witness has identified her signature present on Mahazar marked at Ex.P.2, perhaps she failed to give evidence according to the recitals of the Mahazar Ex.P.2 and her statement marked at Ex.P.4.
As such the learned PP has treated these witnesses PW.2 to P.W.4 and P.W.6 as hostile and cross-examined with the permission of the court.
The efforts of the learned PP completely failed, since the suggestions made to the said witness not admitted by them.
Hence the evidence of P.W.2 to P.W.4 and P.W.6 also not helpful for the prosecution to prove the guilt against the accused.
12. It is obvious to note that the witness P.W.5 Dr.J.V.Shetty being the doctor has treated the victim/complainant Smt.Lakshmamma on 14.04.2018 when she came to hospital with the history of assault.
According to the doctor, she had sustained abrasion on her forehead and small cut injury and swelling present on her left hand.
Accordingly, he has issued wound certificate marked at Ex.P.7.
The entire evidence of the doctor completely denied by the counsel representing the accused.

The police officer P.W.7 Ganganna, retired PSI specifically deposed that on 15.04.2018 at 6.15 p.m,
the complainant came to the police station and lodged complaint.
On the basis of the complaint, he has registered FIR vide Cr.No.148/2018.
Thereafter i.e. on 16.04.2018, he went to the spot and conducted spot Mahazar at the residence of the complainant as shown by the complainant in the presence of panchas as per Ex.P.3.
After completion of both the Mahazar, collected the marriage invitation and marriage photos of the complainant and accused marked at Ex.P.10.
He has recorded statements of C.W.6 to C.W.9 and thereafter handed over further investigation to the witness PW.8 M.Kumar.
The FIR has been marked at Ex.P.9 through the said witness P.W.7.
The evidence of P.W.8 M.Kumar retired PSI discloses that on 20.07.2018 he has collected wound certificate as per Ex.P.7.
As investigation was completed, submitted charge sheet against the accused.

The learned counsel for the accused denied the entire evidence of both P.W.7 and P.W.8, even otherwise the evidence given by the said police official witnesses not corroborate with any one of the independent witness including complainant/victim Smt.Lakshmamma.
So, it is very clear that the prosecution has completely failed in establishing the guilt against the accused beyond reasonable doubt.

As such,
this court has answered the point Nos.1 to 3 in the Negative.
13. Point No.4:

In view of answer of this court on points No.1 to 3, this court proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 506, 307 of IPC.
